\section{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Foundations}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.KKL.Basic
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Foundations: Introduction}
Fourier truncations, stable influences, and coordinate juntas support quantitative approximation on the uniform Boolean cube. The module includes low degree error bounds and counting estimates for bounded-size subsets.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Foundations: Results}

\begin{definition}[Noisy coordinate influence]
\lean{KKL.noisyInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p057-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b008,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b003
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch08-generalized-domains}{pdf-50833afe7403-p009-b003}
\label{KKL.noisyInfluence}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p009-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p018-b003,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p023-b001
}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $i\in[n]$, and $\rho\in\mathbb R$. Define $I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\sum_{S\ni i}\rho^{|S|-1}\widehat f(S)^2$, with natural exponents, including $\rho=0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Low degree Fourier truncation]
\lean{KKL.lowDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b014,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p088-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch08-generalized-domains}{pdf-50833afe7403-p014-b001}
\label{KKL.lowDegreePart}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $k\in\mathbb N$. Define $f^{\le k}(x)=\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[High degree Fourier part]
\lean{KKL.highDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002}
\label{KKL.highDegreePart}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $k\in\mathbb N$. Define $f^{>k}(x)=\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Influential coordinate set]
\lean{KKL.influentialCoords}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b003
}
\label{KKL.influentialCoords}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p022-b003}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $\tau\in\mathbb R$. Define $J_\tau(f)=\{i\in[n]:I_i(f)\ge\tau\}$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real-valued coordinate juntas]
\lean{KKL.IsJunta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p044-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b004
}
\label{KKL.IsJunta}
For every $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and $J\subseteq[n]$, say that $g$ is a $J$-junta if $g(x)=g(y)$ whenever $x_i=y_i$ for every $i\in J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Squared second-norm distance]
\lean{KKL.l2DistSq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\label{KKL.l2DistSq}
For every $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, define $d_2(f,g)^2=\mathbb E_x(f(x)-g(x))^2$ under the uniform distribution on the Boolean cube.
\end{definition}

  {KKL.noisyInfluence}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p057-b001}
\difficulty{4}
\label{KKL.sum_noisyInfluence}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and
$\rho\in\mathbb R$. Then
$\sum_iI_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\rho^{|S|-1}\widehat f(S)^2$, using
natural powers.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total influence sum]
\lean{KKL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_influences}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}

\difficulty{1}
\label{KKL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_influences}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube. Then
$I(f)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(f)$. For a real cube function $h$, define
$I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$
and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Boolean second moment]
\lean{KKL.expect_sq_pm_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_self_pm_one, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne}
\difficulty{3}
\label{KKL.expect_sq_pm_one}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube. Then $\mathbb
Ef^2=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared Fourier weight identity]
\lean{KKL.sum_fourier_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}

\difficulty{3}
\label{KKL.sum_fourier_sq_eq_expect_sq}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube. Then
$\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2=\mathbb Ef^2$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
\label{KKL.low_plus_high_eq}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb
N$, and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Then $f^{\le k}(x)+f^{>k}(x)=f(x)$, where the two parts retain
Fourier coefficients with $|S|\le k$ and $|S|>k$, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coefficients of low degree truncation]
\lean{KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{6}
\label{KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb
N$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. Then $\widehat{f^{\le k}}(S)=\widehat f(S)$ if $|S|\le k$, and
zero otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared truncation error]
\lean{KKL.lowDegree_l2_error}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, KKL.fourierCoeff_highDegreePart, KKL.highDegreePart, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.low_plus_high_eq}
\difficulty{5}
\label{KKL.lowDegree_l2_error}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $k\in\mathbb
N$. Then $\mathbb E(f-f^{\le k})^2=\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and a positive
integer $k$. Then $\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat f(S)^2\le I(f)/k$. For a real cube function $h$,
define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate
$i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}

Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and a positive
integer $k$. Then $\mathbb E(f-f^{\le k})^2\le I(f)/k$. For a real cube function $h$,
define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate
$i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Number of influential coordinates]
\lean{KKL.influential_coords_card}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, KKL.influentialCoords}
\difficulty{4}
\label{KKL.influential_coords_card}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $\tau>0$.
Then $|\{i:I_i(f)\ge\tau\}|\le I(f)/\tau$. For a real cube function $h$, define
$I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$
and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Influential-coordinate approximation]
\lean{KKL.lowDegreePart_depends_on_influential}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{7}
\label{KKL.lowDegreePart_depends_on_influential}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb
N$, and $\tau>0$. There exists $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ depending only on
$J_\tau(f)=\{i:I_i(f)\ge\tau\}$ such that $\mathbb E(f^{\le k}-g)^2\le n\tau$. For a
real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where
$x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Counting subsets of bounded size]
\lean{KKL.card_bounded_subsets_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $s$ be a finite set and let $k$ be a natural number. The number of subsets of $s$
having at most $k$ elements is at most $(|s|+1)^k$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Foundations: Further results}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficients of the high-degree part]
\lean{KKL.fourierCoeff_highDegreePart}
\label{KKL.fourierCoeff_highDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, KKL.highDegreePart}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $d\in\mathbb N$, and let
$T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The Fourier–Walsh coefficient of the part of $f$ supported
on sets of size greater than $d$, at frequency $T$, equals $\widehat f(T)$ if $|T|>d$,
and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Influence of the low-degree truncation]
\lean{KKL.influence_lowDegreePart_le}
\label{KKL.influence_lowDegreePart_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $d\in\mathbb N$, and let
$i$ be a coordinate. The influence of coordinate $i$ on the Fourier truncation of $f$ to
frequencies of size at most $d$ is at most its influence on $f$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Influence after applying the noise operator]
\lean{KKL.influence_noiseOp_le_noisyInfluence}
\label{KKL.influence_noiseOp_le_noisyInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $i$ be a coordinate, and
let $\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\leq\rho\leq1$. The influence of coordinate $i$ on the
noise-operator image of $f$ is at most $\sum_{S\ni i}\rho^{|S|-1}\widehat f(S)^2$, where
the sum ranges over subsets of the coordinate set.
\end{lemma}
